topic.name: Integration Using the Hyperbolic Double-Angle Formulas

question.explanation:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine:

\[ \cos {2\theta}=1-2\sin^2\theta. \]

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

\[ \cosh{2\theta} = 1+ 2\sinh^2{\theta} \]

We can rearrange the above formula as

\[ \sinh^2\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\cosh {2\theta} -1\right ). \]

Letting $\theta = \dfrac{x}{2}$, we have

\[ \sinh^2 \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\cosh {x}-1 \right ). \]

We can now integrate as follows:

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{\ln 4} 16\sinh^2\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) \, \textrm{d}x &= \int_{0}^{\ln 4} 16\cdot \dfrac{1}{2}(\cosh {x}-1) \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= 8\int_{0}^{\ln 4} \left(\cosh{x} - 1 \right) \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=8 \left(\sinh{x} - x \right)\,\bigg|_{0}^{\ln 4} \\[5pt] &= 8\big[\left(\sinh(\ln 4) - \ln{4} \right) - \left(2\sinh 0 - 0 \right)\big] \\[5pt] &= 8\left(\dfrac{e^{\ln 4}-e^{-\ln 4}}{2} - \ln{4}\right)\\[5pt] &=8\left(\dfrac{4-4^{-1}}{2} - 2\ln{2}\right)\\[5pt] &= 15 - 16\ln{2} \end{align*}

example.title: Integrating Expressions Using the Squared Sine Double-Angle Formula

question.explanation:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine:

\[ \cos{2\theta}=\cos^2{\theta} - \sin^2{\theta}. \]

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine: \[ \cosh{2\theta} = \cosh^2 \theta + \sinh^2 \theta . \]

Letting $\theta= \dfrac{x}{3},$ we get

\[ \cosh\left(\dfrac{2x}{3}\right) = \cosh^2 \left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + \sinh^2 \left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right). \]

Substituting this into our integral, we get

\begin{align} \int_{1}^{4} \left(\cosh^2\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + \sinh^2\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) \right)\, \textrm{d}x &= \int_{1}^{4} \cosh\left(\dfrac{2x}{3}\right)\, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=\left.\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\sinh\left(\dfrac{2x}{3}\right)\right)\right|_{1}^{4}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3}{2}\left( \sinh\left(\dfrac{2\cdot 4}{3}\right) - \sinh\left(\dfrac{2\cdot 1}{3}\right) \right)\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{3}{2}}\left(\,\sinh\! \left(\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{8}{3}}\right)-\sinh\! \left(\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{2}{3}}\right)\right). \end{align}

example.title: Integrating Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula for Cosine

question.explanation:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: \[ \cos{2\theta} =2\cos^2 \theta -1 \]

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine: \[ \cosh{2\theta} =2\cosh^2 \theta-1 \]

Rearranging, we have \[ \cosh^2 \theta = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\cosh 2\theta +1 \right). \]

Letting $\theta = \dfrac{4x}{3}$, we have \[ \cosh^2\left(\dfrac{4x}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left( \cosh\left(\dfrac{8x}{3}\right) + 1\right). \] Substituting this into our integral, we get

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{3/2} \left(\cosh^2\left(\dfrac{4x}{3}\right)+ 7x \right) \, \textrm{d}x &= \int_{0}^{3/2} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\cosh\left(\dfrac{8x}{3}\right) + 1\right) + 7x\right) \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{3/2} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\cosh\left(\dfrac{8x}{3}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2} + 7x \right) \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \left.\left(\dfrac{3}{16}\sinh\left(\dfrac{8x}{3}\right)+\dfrac{1}{2}x +\dfrac{7}{2}x^2 \right)\right|_{0}^{3/2}\\[5pt] &= \left[\dfrac{3}{16}\sinh\left(\dfrac{8\cdot (3/2)}{3}\right)+ \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \dfrac{3}{2} +\dfrac{7}{2}\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2 \right] -\left[\dfrac{3}{16}\sinh{0} +0 +\dfrac{7}{2}\cdot 0^2\right]\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{3}{16}}\,\sinh (\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{4}) + \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{69}{8}}. \end{align*}

example.title: Integrating Expressions Using the Squared Cosine Double-Angle Formula

question.explanation:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: \[ \cos{2\theta} =2\cos^2 \theta -1 \]

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine: \[ \cosh{2\theta} =2\cosh^2 \theta-1 \]

Rearranging, we have

\[ \cosh^2 \theta = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\cosh 2\theta +1 \right). \]

Letting $\theta = \dfrac{5x}{3}$, we have \[ \cosh^2\left(\dfrac{5x}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left( \cosh\left(\dfrac{10x}{3}\right) + 1\right). \] Substituting this into our integral, we get

\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{3\pi/10} \left(\cosh^2\left(\dfrac{5x}{3}\right)+ 2 \right) \, \textrm{d}x &= \int_{0}^{3\pi/10} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\cosh\left(\dfrac{10x}{3}\right) + 1\right) + 2\right) \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{3\pi/10} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\cosh\left(\dfrac{10x}{3}\right) + \dfrac{5}{2} \right) \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \left.\left(\dfrac{3}{20}\sinh\left(\dfrac{10x}{3}\right)+\dfrac{5}{2}x \right)\right|_{0}^{3\pi/10}\\[5pt] &= \left[\dfrac{3}{20}\sinh\left(\dfrac{10\cdot(3\pi/10)}{3}\right)+ \dfrac{5}{2}\cdot \dfrac{3\pi}{10} \right] -\left[\dfrac{3}{20}\sinh{0} +0 \right]\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{3}{20}}\,\sinh (\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\pi}) + \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{3\pi}{4}}. \end{align*}

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round your answer.
question.explanation:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: \[ \cos {2\theta}=1-2\sin^2\theta \]

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine: \[ \cosh{2\theta} = 1+ 2\sinh^2{\theta} \]

We can rearrange the above formula as \[ \sinh^2\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\cosh {2\theta} -1\right ). \]

Letting $\theta = \dfrac{x}{2}$, we have \[ \sinh^2 \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\cosh {x}-1 \right ). \]

We can now integrate as follows: \begin{align*} \int_{0}^{\pi} 8\sinh^2\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) \, \textrm{d}x &= \int_{0}^{\pi} 8\cdot \dfrac{1}{2}(\cosh {x}-1) \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= 4\int_{0}^{\pi} \left(\cosh{x} - 1 \right) \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=4 \left(\sinh{x} - x \right)\,\bigg|_{0}^{\pi} \\[5pt] &= 4\big[\left(\sinh\pi - \pi \right) - \left(\sinh 0 - 0 \right)\big] \\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{4} \sinh\left(\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\pi}\right)-\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{4\pi} \end{align*}
